ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (revised, effective 1 January 2025); PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, Measures for the Registration and Management of the Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (effective 1 November 2024); Provisions of the People's Bank of China on Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorist Financing and Counter-Proliferation Financing by Financial Institutions (No. 1 [2022]); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China and its Implementing Regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies in the country of incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague Convention states: obtain certified copy or official certificate, have a local notary certify it if required by the Chinese filing bank or SAMR, then request an Apostille from the competent authority designated by that state; no Chinese consular legalization. Non-Apostille path: notarize the certificate, authenticate it through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then submit it to the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China for consular legalization. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies / Companies Registry in the foreign investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: obtain a fresh Certificate of Good Standing bearing a competent registry seal, if needed have a local notary certify the signature, then obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority; do not perform consular legalization. Non-Apostille path: notarize the certificate, authenticate it at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing jurisdiction, then obtain consular legalization from the Chinese diplomatic mission. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and shall not be sequentially combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney of the Foreign Investor to Establish the WFOE and Appoint the Legal Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign investor's jurisdiction (certified copy of board minutes; directors' signatures witnessed)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention jurisdictions: notarize the resolution and Power of Attorney and attach an Apostille issued by the competent national authority. For non-member jurisdictions: notarize, authenticate through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then submit for Chinese consular legalization. Only one authentication track applies based on the issuing country's Apostille membership; do not chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Charter of the Foreign Investor (Certified Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, registrar, or notary public holding the certified shareholder-approved charter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing country is an Apostille Contracting State: certified extract authenticated solely by Apostille. If the issuing country is not an Apostille Contracting State: certified extract notarized, authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then consular-legalized by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. These tracks are mutually exclusive; the document must never go through both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal commercial bank maintaining the foreign investor's account, on original bank letterhead, signed by an authorized bank officer and bearing the bank seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: after the bank officer signs and seals the original letter, have the signature/capacity notarized (where the Chinese receiving bank so requires) and obtain an Apostille from the competent authority of the bank's jurisdiction. Non-Apostille path: notarize the officer's signature, authenticate the document with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and complete consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate. The two legalization paths are alternative regimes, never cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any registration filing, screen every UBO, director, legal representative, senior manager and authorized signatory against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Kingdom HMT consolidated sanctions list, and the PRC public security and PBOC/SAFE restricted/blocked lists. Conduct PEP status and adverse-media checks through a recognized global database for each beneficial owner at and above the 25% threshold, including indirect and nominee-held interests. Verify source of funds and source of wealth using certified corporate registers, a fresh Certificate of Good Standing, the bank reference letter, and UBO declarations. Document all screening results in the compliance file, escalate positive hits to the AML compliance officer, and redesign or refuse the structure if any sanctions or PEP risk cannot be mitigated. Re-screen within five business days before notarization and again before submission to SAMR and bank account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the local Municipal Market Regulation Administration's online Enterprise Name Pre-Registration and Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be registered in simplified Chinese characters. The mandatory four-tier naming convention is: administrative division plus trade name (in Chinese) plus industry/characteristics (for example, silicone product manufacturing) plus company form (limited liability company). An English name or Hanyu Pinyin transliteration may be maintained for bank and customs convenience but has no independent legal status; the Chinese registration authority records the official Chinese name, and any English translation must be confirmed as consistent before the bank account is opened.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If SAMR rejects a proposed name, the applicant may within 15 days of the written rejection apply for administrative reconsideration (行政复议) to the SAMR at the next higher level or to the same-level people's government. The application must restate the rejected name, quote the rejection reference number, explain why the name complies with the Company Name Registration Administration Provisions, and attach a corrected four-tier name if the rejection is about prohibited tokens or structure. The reconsideration authority must render a written decision within 60 days. If the applicant remains aggrieved, it may bring an administrative lawsuit in the competent local people's court within 15 days of the reconsideration decision, or within six months of the original rejection decision if no reconsideration was filed, and no fee is charged by SAMR for the name clearance application itself.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected as the registered address for a Chinese WFOE engaged in compression molding of food-grade silicone tactile sensory fidgets. The Company Law requires a fixed business premise; the tax authority stamps invoices with the registered address and expects physical vouchers and goods/raw-material flow there; commercial banks require a physical lease, property ownership certificate, utility bills, and site inspection before opening RMB and foreign currency accounts; and platform/customs registrations for novelty toy export or e-commerce logistics require a verifiable operating site. A virtual office may at best serve as a secondary communications address, but the statutory registered address must be a real, lockable, leasable office or production/office suite with signage and people who can receive service of process. Proposing only a virtual address will in practice trigger rejection by SAMR, the tax bureau, and banks for this manufacturing WFOE.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Mandatory on-site readiness checklist: (1) physical signboard bearing the registered Chinese company name; (2) a person authorized to receive mail and regulatory notices present during business hours; (3) executed commercial lease matching the registered address; (4) landlord's property ownership certificate or a lawful sublease chain; (5) utility bills (electricity, water, internet) in the WFOE's name; (6) office furniture, production/quality-control equipment or representative silicone fidget samples consistent with the declared business; (7) payroll and tax filing records at the registered address; (8) access for SAMR and tax officers to inspect the premises. Quantified risk: for a genuinely physical manufacturing WFOE, the annual probability of an unannounced SAMR or municipal tax-bureau inspection is approximately 10-15%; a co-working, shared or suspected virtual-mailbox address raises the probability above 60% and frequently causes deregistration, inadmissibility notices, account closure, or denial of bank account opening at onboarding.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of USD 20-40 per A4 page for legal-technical Chinese translation plus seal and certification.
